details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

cna.title: Ca-certificates: distrust emudhra intermediate ca certificates due to security concerns

descriptions.value:
The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates RPM packages, included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL client using system CA store and cause such clients to connect to malicious sites.

Due to inability to only distrust specific intermediate certificates in all clients using the system CA store, root CA certificates of authorities that signed weak intermediate CA certificates are being removed.

supportingMedia.value:
Externally-Generated Error Message Containing Sensitive Information vulnerability in plug_crypto in elixir-plug plug_crypto allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to expose the secret key base through application logs via a wrong-typed argument. Every public function in Plug.Crypto validates argument types in a function-head guard. A failed guard makes the Erlang VM raise FunctionClauseError with the actual argument values in the top stack frame, so the secret key base, a derived key, or the value an API key is compared against lands in that frame. The library's rescue blocks and Plug.Crypto.prune_args_from_stacktrace/1 only reach exceptions raised inside a function body, so they never see a guard failure. Plug.Cowboy and Bandit write the frame to the error log and attach it as crash_reason Logger metadata, which error trackers forward.

Two entry points take request data. Plug.Crypto.verify/4 exposes the secret key base when the token is neither a binary nor nil, which Phoenix.Token.verify/4 reaches because it forwards the token unguarded. Plug.Crypto.secure_compare/2 exposes the other operand when one side is not a binary, as happens when a missing request header yields nil. Reading the leaked value needs separate access to the logs or the error tracker, so the request alone does not disclose the secret to the attacker.

This issue affects plug: from 1.6.3 before 1.7.0; plug_crypto: from 1.0.0 before 2.2.1.

supportingMedia.value:
Check argument types in the calling code before entering Plug.Crypto, so no head guard ever fails. Pass a token to Phoenix.Token.verify/4, Phoenix.Token.decrypt/4, Plug.Crypto.verify/4 or Plug.Crypto.decrypt/4 only when is_binary(token) holds, and treat anything else as an invalid token. Call Plug.Crypto.secure_compare/2 only when both operands are binaries, treating a missing header or parameter as a failed comparison rather than passing nil.

Where the leaked value matters more than the crash, configuring the error tracker to drop stack-frame arguments also keeps the secret out of the forwarded report. For Sentry this means not sending vars with the crash report. This narrows exposure but leaves the value in the local error log.

1. Run an application that depends on plug_crypto and exposes a route calling Phoenix.Token.verify(secret_key_base, "user auth", conn.params["token"]), plus a route calling Plug.Crypto.secure_compare(List.first(get_req_header(conn, "x-api-key")), api_key).
  2. Send GET /verify?token[]=x. Plug.Parsers yields a list for the bracket syntax, so the token argument is a list.
  3. Observe the 500 response and read the error log. The top frame prints Plug.Crypto.verify("SECRET_KEY_BASE_...", "user auth", ["x"], []) with the secret key base in full, and the same frame is attached as crash_reason Logger metadata.
  4. Send GET /api with no x-api-key header. The header lookup yields nil, and the frame prints Plug.Crypto.secure_compare(nil, "<configured API key>").
  5. A JSON body of {"token": 123} to the first route gives the same result with an integer argument.

supportingMedia.value:
1. Type checks in function-head guards. Every public function in Plug.Crypto validates its arguments in a head guard, for example secure_compare/2 with when is_binary(left) and is_binary(right) and verify/4 with when is_binary(key_base) and is_binary(salt) and is_binary(token).

2. The VM builds the error, not the library. When no clause matches, the Erlang VM raises FunctionClauseError and the top stack frame holds the actual argument values. The library's rescue ... reraise blocks and Plug.Crypto.prune_args_from_stacktrace/1 only apply to exceptions raised inside a function body, so a guard failure never reaches them. In plug_crypto the same commit that added prune_args_from_stacktrace/1 also added these guards.

3. Which value leaks. verify/4 and sign/4 put the secret key base in the frame. decrypt/4 has no is_binary(token) guard on its main clause, so the key is derived first and the failing guard belongs to MessageEncryptor.decrypt/4, placing the derived 32-byte key in the frame. secure_compare/2 places the other operand in the frame, which is the server-side secret when a request value is nil.

4. The frame reaches logs and error trackers. Plug.Cowboy and Bandit write the formatted frame, arguments included, to the error log and attach it as crash_reason Logger metadata. Error trackers forward it; Sentry's handler sends crash reports by default and serializes frame arguments as vars.

cna.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in CGM CLININET

descriptions.description: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

descriptions.value:
CGM CLININET is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) due to improper neutralization of user-supplied data. A remote unauthenticated attacker can craft a malicious URL containing JavaScript or HTML code, which is executed in the victim's browser when the URL is visited, allowing the attacker to steal session cookies and perform actions on behalf of the victim within the application.



The vulnerability was confirmed to affect versions up to 2026.MS3 but later versions may also be vulnerable.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's memory limit handling during request parsing. PHP records certain state as ready for use before all required memory allocations complete. If an allocation fails due to memory exhaustion, the incomplete state is not rolled back. Subsequent cleanup operations treat the uninitialized memory as valid, leading to memory corruption. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via crafted HTTP requests to achieve remote code execution against mod_php with default configuration, and against FPM through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Rated Important. An unauthenticated remote attacker could corrupt engine memory and potentially execute arbitrary code, but reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing. Standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM rather than mod_php. PHP-FPM workers exit on early initialization failures before reaching the corrupted structures, so remote code execution is difficult in practice and typically requires non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution.

vulnerabilities.title: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's error handling and worker process state management. PHP contains error handling, object, and extension state that is retained by the process but points to memory owned by a single request. A fatal error can interrupt an operation or cleanup phase before that state is reset. If PHP catches the failure and continues cleanup, or reuses the persistent worker for a subsequent request, a later operation may act on the stale state after its underlying memory has been released. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to achieve use-after-free and remote code execution against mod_php. FPM is conditionally affected through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory corruption leading to potential arbitrary code execution. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, PHP applications exposed to public networks handle incoming requests directly, so no prior authentication is needed to reach the vulnerable code. Exploitation requires hitting a precise out-of-memory condition during request processing, which keeps this below Critical.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's memory limit handling during request parsing. PHP records certain state as ready for use before all required memory allocations complete. If an allocation fails due to memory exhaustion, the incomplete state is not rolled back. Subsequent cleanup operations treat the uninitialized memory as valid, leading to memory corruption. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via crafted HTTP requests to achieve remote code execution against mod_php with default configuration, and against FPM through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Rated Important. An unauthenticated remote attacker could corrupt engine memory and potentially execute arbitrary code, but reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing. Standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM rather than mod_php. PHP-FPM workers exit on early initialization failures before reaching the corrupted structures, so remote code execution is difficult in practice and typically requires non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution.

vulnerabilities.title: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's error handling and worker process state management. PHP contains error handling, object, and extension state that is retained by the process but points to memory owned by a single request. A fatal error can interrupt an operation or cleanup phase before that state is reset. If PHP catches the failure and continues cleanup, or reuses the persistent worker for a subsequent request, a later operation may act on the stale state after its underlying memory has been released. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to achieve use-after-free and remote code execution against mod_php. FPM is conditionally affected through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory corruption leading to potential arbitrary code execution. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, PHP applications exposed to public networks handle incoming requests directly, so no prior authentication is needed to reach the vulnerable code. Exploitation requires hitting a precise out-of-memory condition during request processing, which keeps this below Critical.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's memory limit handling during request parsing. PHP records certain state as ready for use before all required memory allocations complete. If an allocation fails due to memory exhaustion, the incomplete state is not rolled back. Subsequent cleanup operations treat the uninitialized memory as valid, leading to memory corruption. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via crafted HTTP requests to achieve remote code execution against mod_php with default configuration, and against FPM through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Rated Important. An unauthenticated remote attacker could corrupt engine memory and potentially execute arbitrary code, but reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing. Standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM rather than mod_php. PHP-FPM workers exit on early initialization failures before reaching the corrupted structures, so remote code execution is difficult in practice and typically requires non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's error handling and worker process state management. PHP contains error handling, object, and extension state that is retained by the process but points to memory owned by a single request. A fatal error can interrupt an operation or cleanup phase before that state is reset. If PHP catches the failure and continues cleanup, or reuses the persistent worker for a subsequent request, a later operation may act on the stale state after its underlying memory has been released. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to achieve use-after-free and remote code execution against mod_php. FPM is conditionally affected through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory corruption leading to potential arbitrary code execution. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, PHP applications exposed to public networks handle incoming requests directly, so no prior authentication is needed to reach the vulnerable code. Exploitation requires hitting a precise out-of-memory condition during request processing, which keeps this below Critical.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's memory limit handling during request parsing. PHP records certain state as ready for use before all required memory allocations complete. If an allocation fails due to memory exhaustion, the incomplete state is not rolled back. Subsequent cleanup operations treat the uninitialized memory as valid, leading to memory corruption. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via crafted HTTP requests to achieve remote code execution against mod_php with default configuration, and against FPM through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Rated Important. An unauthenticated remote attacker could corrupt engine memory and potentially execute arbitrary code, but reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing. Standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM rather than mod_php. PHP-FPM workers exit on early initialization failures before reaching the corrupted structures, so remote code execution is difficult in practice and typically requires non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's error handling and worker process state management. PHP contains error handling, object, and extension state that is retained by the process but points to memory owned by a single request. A fatal error can interrupt an operation or cleanup phase before that state is reset. If PHP catches the failure and continues cleanup, or reuses the persistent worker for a subsequent request, a later operation may act on the stale state after its underlying memory has been released. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to achieve use-after-free and remote code execution against mod_php. FPM is conditionally affected through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory corruption leading to potential arbitrary code execution. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, PHP applications exposed to public networks handle incoming requests directly, so no prior authentication is needed to reach the vulnerable code. Exploitation requires hitting a precise out-of-memory condition during request processing, which keeps this below Critical.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. An unauthenticated remote attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted request to an affected Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) server endpoint. Due to a lack of recursion depth limits when parsing deeply nested XML elements, processing such requests exhausts system stack memory and crashes the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An important-impact denial-of-service flaw exists in PHP's SOAP extension. When a SoapServer endpoint processes a specially crafted, deeply nested SOAP XML request, unbounded recursion in XML cleanup (and related decode/WSDL helpers) can exhaust the process stack and crash the PHP worker. Exploitation requires a reachable SoapServer that loads ext/soap; typical PHP applications that do not enable the SOAP extension or expose SoapServer are not affected by this attack path. Under PHP-FPM, repeated requests can exhaust the worker pool and take the application offline. Red Hat enterprise hardenings such as ASLR, NX, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and SELinux do not mitigate this stack-exhaustion DoS.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

If SoapServer is unused, disable or remove the SOAP extension (php-soap / extension=soap) so the vulnerable parser is not loaded. Restrict any exposed SoapServer endpoints to trusted clients using a host firewall or network segmentation. Process and cgroup resource limits may contain host impact but do not prevent PHP-FPM worker crashes or pool exhaustion from crafted nested SOAP requests.

vulnerabilities.title: php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's memory limit handling during request parsing. PHP records certain state as ready for use before all required memory allocations complete. If an allocation fails due to memory exhaustion, the incomplete state is not rolled back. Subsequent cleanup operations treat the uninitialized memory as valid, leading to memory corruption. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via crafted HTTP requests to achieve remote code execution against mod_php with default configuration, and against FPM through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Rated Important. An unauthenticated remote attacker could corrupt engine memory and potentially execute arbitrary code, but reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing. Standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM rather than mod_php. PHP-FPM workers exit on early initialization failures before reaching the corrupted structures, so remote code execution is difficult in practice and typically requires non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution.
notes.title: Statement

vulnerabilities.title: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's error handling and worker process state management. PHP contains error handling, object, and extension state that is retained by the process but points to memory owned by a single request. A fatal error can interrupt an operation or cleanup phase before that state is reset. If PHP catches the failure and continues cleanup, or reuses the persistent worker for a subsequent request, a later operation may act on the stale state after its underlying memory has been released. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to achieve use-after-free and remote code execution against mod_php. FPM is conditionally affected through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory corruption leading to potential arbitrary code execution. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, PHP applications exposed to public networks handle incoming requests directly, so no prior authentication is needed to reach the vulnerable code. Exploitation requires hitting a precise out-of-memory condition during request processing, which keeps this below Critical.

An update for the php:7.4 module is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

notes.text:
PHP is an HTML-embedded scripting language commonly used with the Apache HTTP Server.

Security Fix(es):

* php: php: Out-of-bounds read via empty HTTP redirect Location header (CVE-2026-93682)

* php: PHP: Archive entry injection via integer overflow in TAR parser (CVE-2026-6103)

* php: PHP: Denial of Service via heap buffer overflow in SOAP client (CVE-2025-14181)

* php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser (CVE-2026-91765)

* php: php: Credential disclosure via cross-origin HTTP redirects (CVE-2026-91766)

* php: php: Information disclosure via crafted TLS server certificate (CVE-2026-91767)

* php: php: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in mysqlnd wire protocol parser (CVE-2025-1218)

* php: php: Access control bypass via partial IPv6 address comparison (CVE-2026-91768)

* php: php: Information disclosure via out-of-bounds read in stream filters (CVE-2026-92842)

* php: php: Server impersonation via Common Name fallback in TLS verification (CVE-2026-91769)

* php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE (CVE-2026-109618)

* php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free (CVE-2026-109619)

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. The MySQL Native Driver (mysqlnd) wire protocol parser fails to verify that an incoming packet contains enough bytes before reading its fields. A malicious or compromised database server can send a truncated packet, causing the client application to read past the buffer boundary. This issue can lead to a process crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS), or potentially leak sensitive memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: php: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in mysqlnd wire protocol parser
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This issue is rated Low for Red Hat customers because exploitation requires a PHP application using mysqlnd to communicate with a malicious or compromised MySQL server, and the practical impact is an out-of-bounds read that primarily crashes the client process. Confidentiality and integrity impact are not established for Red Hat product use. Applications that connect only to trusted database servers are not practically exposed.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. A malicious server can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by exploiting an improper buffer size check in the Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) client during HTTP response parsing. When responding to a request, the server can supply crafted data that triggers an integer calculation issue, causing the client to allocate an undersized memory buffer. As the client writes incoming data past the allocated space, a heap-based buffer overflow occurs, leading to an application crash or potential memory corruption.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: PHP: Denial of Service via heap buffer overflow in SOAP client
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Moderate because a malicious SOAP server can trigger unreliable buffer-size checks in PHP's SOAP HTTP client, leading to a heap buffer overflow that primarily causes denial of service and may allow limited memory corruption. Attack complexity is high because the overflow depends on compiler behavior and very large responses.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

Set a conservative PHP memory_limit so oversized SOAP responses fail before overflow conditions are reached. Restrict SoapClient endpoints to trusted servers over TLS and isolate SOAP traffic.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. An integer overflow vulnerability in the Phar extension occurs when parsing TAR archive headers containing excessively large size fields. An attacker can exploit this issue by supplying a specially crafted archive file to an application that processes TAR archives, causing the parser to miscalculate data boundaries and treat file content as valid header data. This allows an attacker to inject unauthorized entries that the application extracts as authentic files, potentially leading to unauthorized data modification.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: PHP: Archive entry injection via integer overflow in TAR parser
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Moderate because a crafted TAR archive can cause PHP's Phar TAR parser to mishandle oversized size fields and inject archive entries, undermining integrity of extracted content. Exploitation requires an application to open or extract an untrusted archive (for example via PharData or phar://).
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. An unauthenticated remote attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted request to an affected Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) server endpoint. Due to a lack of recursion depth limits when parsing deeply nested XML elements, processing such requests exhausts system stack memory and crashes the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An important-impact denial-of-service flaw exists in PHP's SOAP extension. When a SoapServer endpoint processes a specially crafted, deeply nested SOAP XML request, unbounded recursion in XML cleanup (and related decode/WSDL helpers) can exhaust the process stack and crash the PHP worker. Exploitation requires a reachable SoapServer that loads ext/soap; typical PHP applications that do not enable the SOAP extension or expose SoapServer are not affected by this attack path. Under PHP-FPM, repeated requests can exhaust the worker pool and take the application offline. Red Hat enterprise hardenings such as ASLR, NX, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and SELinux do not mitigate this stack-exhaustion DoS.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

If SoapServer is unused, disable or remove the SOAP extension (php-soap / extension=soap) so the vulnerable parser is not loaded. Restrict any exposed SoapServer endpoints to trusted clients using a host firewall or network segmentation. Process and cgroup resource limits may contain host impact but do not prevent PHP-FPM worker crashes or pool exhaustion from crafted nested SOAP requests.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. When following a redirect, the built-in HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) stream wrapper forwards sensitive request headers—such as authentication tokens and session cookies—unchanged, even when directed to a different host, port, or unencrypted connection. A malicious server capable of steering redirects can exploit this flaw to capture sensitive credentials intended only for the original destination.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: php: Credential disclosure via cross-origin HTTP redirects
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Moderate because PHP's HTTP stream wrapper can forward Authorization, Cookie, and Proxy-Authorization headers across cross-origin redirects, exposing credentials to an attacker-controlled redirect target. Attack complexity is elevated because the initial destination must issue a redirect that the client follows.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. When validating secure connections using Transport Layer Security (TLS), an error in how wildcard domain names in server certificates are verified can lead to an out-of-bounds memory read. A malicious server presenting a specially crafted certificate can exploit this issue against a connecting PHP client. This flaw primarily leads to information disclosure, potentially exposing sensitive data stored in application memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: php: Information disclosure via crafted TLS server certificate
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Moderate because a PHP TLS client that verifies peer names can suffer an out-of-bounds read when a server presents a crafted wildcard certificate, crashing the client process (denial of service). The GHSA analysis indicates the scan result is used only for accept/reject and is not returned to the attacker, so Red Hat scores availability impact without confidentiality impact. Exploitation requires the client to connect to a server that can present such a certificate (malicious server or compromised/trusted CA path).
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. The access control check for Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) addresses in the FastCGI implementation compares only the first 12 bytes of a 16-byte address instead of the complete address. An attacker on an adjacent network with an address sharing the first 96 bits with an authorized client can bypass network access restrictions to reach the FastCGI endpoint, potentially leading to unauthorized information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: php: Access control bypass via partial IPv6 address comparison
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact because exploitation requires PHP-FPM to be configured to listen on an IPv6 network socket, whereas Red Hat Enterprise Linux configurations typically use local UNIX domain sockets or loopback interfaces. Furthermore, an attacker must be located on an adjacent network capable of sourcing an IPv6 address sharing the first 96 bits with an authorized client. Systems communicating strictly through local UNIX sockets or isolated via network filtering are not exposed to unauthorized FastCGI access.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Configure PHP-FPM to communicate over a local UNIX domain socket or enforce IPv6 access controls using host-based firewall rules.

1. Local UNIX domain socket configuration (for deployments where the web server and PHP-FPM reside on the same host):
Edit `/etc/php-fpm.d/www.conf` to set:
listen = /run/php-fpm/www.sock

Configure the upstream web server (such as Apache HTTP Server or NGINX) to route FastCGI requests via the UNIX socket path instead of TCP.

Apply the configuration by restarting the service:
systemctl restart php-fpm

2. Firewall filtering (if PHP-FPM must listen over a TCP network port):
Restrict access to the FastCGI port using firewalld to ensure exact 128-bit IPv6 address matching:
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv6" source address="<ALLOWED_IPV6_HOST>/128" port port="9000" protocol="tcp" accept'
firewall-cmd --reload

Caveats: Switching to a UNIX domain socket requires aligning FastCGI proxy parameters in the upstream web server. Applying firewall rules may block legitimate traffic if authorized client IPv6 addresses change dynamically.
Warning: Restarting php-fpm will terminate active FastCGI connections and temporarily disrupt processing of PHP requests.

vulnerabilities.title: php: php: Access control bypass via partial IPv6 address comparison

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. This vulnerability allows server impersonation and potential information disclosure during Transport Layer Security (TLS) connections. When verifying peer certificates, PHP improperly falls back to matching the Common Name (CN) if no Subject Alternative Name (SAN) matches the requested hostname. An attacker could exploit this flaw by presenting a certificate trusted for another domain whose CN matches the target, enabling them to impersonate a legitimate server and intercept sensitive data.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: php: Server impersonation via Common Name fallback in TLS verification
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated as Moderate impact because an attacker must achieve an active man-in-the-middle network position and present a trusted certificate possessing a matching Common Name alongside disparate Subject Alternative Names. Exposure in Red Hat environments is restricted to outbound TLS client connections established via PHP streams; inbound application traffic processed by PHP-FPM or mod_php is unaffected. Furthermore, public certificate authorities generally disallow conflicting identity combinations, limiting the real-world attack surface.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. When processing certain conversion stream filters with line-break settings containing a null byte, the filter duplicates the string but retains the original length rather than the truncated size. An attacker who can influence filter options could exploit this out-of-bounds read, leading to information disclosure by leaking sensitive heap memory contents into the output stream.

notes.text: php: php: Information disclosure via out-of-bounds read in stream filters
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate severity because exploitation requires an application to process untrusted input that controls specific stream filter configuration parameters, namely line-break character options containing null bytes. In standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, applications rarely expose filter instantiation parameters directly to unauthenticated external users. While an out-of-bounds read can leak adjacent memory data into the processed stream, it does not enable arbitrary code execution or system modification.

vulnerabilities.title: php: php: Information disclosure via out-of-bounds read in stream filters

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. When the HTTP stream wrapper processes a redirect response containing an empty Location header, an out-of-bounds read occurs by accessing memory beyond the allocated buffer. A malicious server can exploit this flaw to influence the client's redirect target path, potentially routing subsequent requests to unintended locations based on adjacent heap memory.

vulnerabilities.title: php: php: Out-of-bounds read via empty HTTP redirect Location header

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's memory limit handling during request parsing. PHP records certain state as ready for use before all required memory allocations complete. If an allocation fails due to memory exhaustion, the incomplete state is not rolled back. Subsequent cleanup operations treat the uninitialized memory as valid, leading to memory corruption. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via crafted HTTP requests to achieve remote code execution against mod_php with default configuration, and against FPM through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Rated Important. An unauthenticated remote attacker could corrupt engine memory and potentially execute arbitrary code, but reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing. Standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM rather than mod_php. PHP-FPM workers exit on early initialization failures before reaching the corrupted structures, so remote code execution is difficult in practice and typically requires non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution.

vulnerabilities.title: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's error handling and worker process state management. PHP contains error handling, object, and extension state that is retained by the process but points to memory owned by a single request. A fatal error can interrupt an operation or cleanup phase before that state is reset. If PHP catches the failure and continues cleanup, or reuses the persistent worker for a subsequent request, a later operation may act on the stale state after its underlying memory has been released. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to achieve use-after-free and remote code execution against mod_php. FPM is conditionally affected through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory corruption leading to potential arbitrary code execution. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, PHP applications exposed to public networks handle incoming requests directly, so no prior authentication is needed to reach the vulnerable code. Exploitation requires hitting a precise out-of-memory condition during request processing, which keeps this below Critical.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. An unauthenticated remote attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted request to an affected Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) server endpoint. Due to a lack of recursion depth limits when parsing deeply nested XML elements, processing such requests exhausts system stack memory and crashes the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An important-impact denial-of-service flaw exists in PHP's SOAP extension. When a SoapServer endpoint processes a specially crafted, deeply nested SOAP XML request, unbounded recursion in XML cleanup (and related decode/WSDL helpers) can exhaust the process stack and crash the PHP worker. Exploitation requires a reachable SoapServer that loads ext/soap; typical PHP applications that do not enable the SOAP extension or expose SoapServer are not affected by this attack path. Under PHP-FPM, repeated requests can exhaust the worker pool and take the application offline. Red Hat enterprise hardenings such as ASLR, NX, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and SELinux do not mitigate this stack-exhaustion DoS.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

If SoapServer is unused, disable or remove the SOAP extension (php-soap / extension=soap) so the vulnerable parser is not loaded. Restrict any exposed SoapServer endpoints to trusted clients using a host firewall or network segmentation. Process and cgroup resource limits may contain host impact but do not prevent PHP-FPM worker crashes or pool exhaustion from crafted nested SOAP requests.

vulnerabilities.title: php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's memory limit handling during request parsing. PHP records certain state as ready for use before all required memory allocations complete. If an allocation fails due to memory exhaustion, the incomplete state is not rolled back. Subsequent cleanup operations treat the uninitialized memory as valid, leading to memory corruption. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via crafted HTTP requests to achieve remote code execution against mod_php with default configuration, and against FPM through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Rated Important. An unauthenticated remote attacker could corrupt engine memory and potentially execute arbitrary code, but reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing. Standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM rather than mod_php. PHP-FPM workers exit on early initialization failures before reaching the corrupted structures, so remote code execution is difficult in practice and typically requires non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution.

vulnerabilities.title: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's error handling and worker process state management. PHP contains error handling, object, and extension state that is retained by the process but points to memory owned by a single request. A fatal error can interrupt an operation or cleanup phase before that state is reset. If PHP catches the failure and continues cleanup, or reuses the persistent worker for a subsequent request, a later operation may act on the stale state after its underlying memory has been released. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to achieve use-after-free and remote code execution against mod_php. FPM is conditionally affected through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory corruption leading to potential arbitrary code execution. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, PHP applications exposed to public networks handle incoming requests directly, so no prior authentication is needed to reach the vulnerable code. Exploitation requires hitting a precise out-of-memory condition during request processing, which keeps this below Critical.

An update for the php:8.2 module is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
PHP is an HTML-embedded scripting language commonly used with the Apache HTTP Server.

Security Fix(es):

* php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser (CVE-2026-91765)

* php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE (CVE-2026-109618)

* php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free (CVE-2026-109619)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. An unauthenticated remote attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted request to an affected Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) server endpoint. Due to a lack of recursion depth limits when parsing deeply nested XML elements, processing such requests exhausts system stack memory and crashes the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An important-impact denial-of-service flaw exists in PHP's SOAP extension. When a SoapServer endpoint processes a specially crafted, deeply nested SOAP XML request, unbounded recursion in XML cleanup (and related decode/WSDL helpers) can exhaust the process stack and crash the PHP worker. Exploitation requires a reachable SoapServer that loads ext/soap; typical PHP applications that do not enable the SOAP extension or expose SoapServer are not affected by this attack path. Under PHP-FPM, repeated requests can exhaust the worker pool and take the application offline. Red Hat enterprise hardenings such as ASLR, NX, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and SELinux do not mitigate this stack-exhaustion DoS.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

If SoapServer is unused, disable or remove the SOAP extension (php-soap / extension=soap) so the vulnerable parser is not loaded. Restrict any exposed SoapServer endpoints to trusted clients using a host firewall or network segmentation. Process and cgroup resource limits may contain host impact but do not prevent PHP-FPM worker crashes or pool exhaustion from crafted nested SOAP requests.

vulnerabilities.title: php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's memory limit handling during request parsing. PHP records certain state as ready for use before all required memory allocations complete. If an allocation fails due to memory exhaustion, the incomplete state is not rolled back. Subsequent cleanup operations treat the uninitialized memory as valid, leading to memory corruption. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via crafted HTTP requests to achieve remote code execution against mod_php with default configuration, and against FPM through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Rated Important. An unauthenticated remote attacker could corrupt engine memory and potentially execute arbitrary code, but reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing. Standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM rather than mod_php. PHP-FPM workers exit on early initialization failures before reaching the corrupted structures, so remote code execution is difficult in practice and typically requires non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution.

vulnerabilities.title: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's error handling and worker process state management. PHP contains error handling, object, and extension state that is retained by the process but points to memory owned by a single request. A fatal error can interrupt an operation or cleanup phase before that state is reset. If PHP catches the failure and continues cleanup, or reuses the persistent worker for a subsequent request, a later operation may act on the stale state after its underlying memory has been released. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to achieve use-after-free and remote code execution against mod_php. FPM is conditionally affected through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory corruption leading to potential arbitrary code execution. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, PHP applications exposed to public networks handle incoming requests directly, so no prior authentication is needed to reach the vulnerable code. Exploitation requires hitting a precise out-of-memory condition during request processing, which keeps this below Critical.

notes.text:
PHP is an HTML-embedded scripting language commonly used with the Apache HTTP Server.

* php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser (CVE-2026-91765)

* php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE (CVE-2026-109618)

* php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free (CVE-2026-109619)

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. An unauthenticated remote attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted request to an affected Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) server endpoint. Due to a lack of recursion depth limits when parsing deeply nested XML elements, processing such requests exhausts system stack memory and crashes the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An important-impact denial-of-service flaw exists in PHP's SOAP extension. When a SoapServer endpoint processes a specially crafted, deeply nested SOAP XML request, unbounded recursion in XML cleanup (and related decode/WSDL helpers) can exhaust the process stack and crash the PHP worker. Exploitation requires a reachable SoapServer that loads ext/soap; typical PHP applications that do not enable the SOAP extension or expose SoapServer are not affected by this attack path. Under PHP-FPM, repeated requests can exhaust the worker pool and take the application offline. Red Hat enterprise hardenings such as ASLR, NX, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and SELinux do not mitigate this stack-exhaustion DoS.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

If SoapServer is unused, disable or remove the SOAP extension (php-soap / extension=soap) so the vulnerable parser is not loaded. Restrict any exposed SoapServer endpoints to trusted clients using a host firewall or network segmentation. Process and cgroup resource limits may contain host impact but do not prevent PHP-FPM worker crashes or pool exhaustion from crafted nested SOAP requests.

vulnerabilities.title: php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's memory limit handling during request parsing. PHP records certain state as ready for use before all required memory allocations complete. If an allocation fails due to memory exhaustion, the incomplete state is not rolled back. Subsequent cleanup operations treat the uninitialized memory as valid, leading to memory corruption. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via crafted HTTP requests to achieve remote code execution against mod_php with default configuration, and against FPM through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Rated Important. An unauthenticated remote attacker could corrupt engine memory and potentially execute arbitrary code, but reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing. Standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM rather than mod_php. PHP-FPM workers exit on early initialization failures before reaching the corrupted structures, so remote code execution is difficult in practice and typically requires non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution.

vulnerabilities.title: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's error handling and worker process state management. PHP contains error handling, object, and extension state that is retained by the process but points to memory owned by a single request. A fatal error can interrupt an operation or cleanup phase before that state is reset. If PHP catches the failure and continues cleanup, or reuses the persistent worker for a subsequent request, a later operation may act on the stale state after its underlying memory has been released. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to achieve use-after-free and remote code execution against mod_php. FPM is conditionally affected through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory corruption leading to potential arbitrary code execution. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, PHP applications exposed to public networks handle incoming requests directly, so no prior authentication is needed to reach the vulnerable code. Exploitation requires hitting a precise out-of-memory condition during request processing, which keeps this below Critical.

An update for php8.4 is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
PHP is an HTML-embedded scripting language. PHP attempts to make it easy for developers to write dynamically generated web pages. PHP also offers built-in database integration for several commercial and non-commercial database management systems, so writing a database-enabled webpage with PHP is fairly simple. The most common use of PHP coding is probably as a replacement for CGI scripts.

Security Fix(es):

* php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser (CVE-2026-91765)

* php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE (CVE-2026-109618)

* php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free (CVE-2026-109619)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. An unauthenticated remote attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted request to an affected Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) server endpoint. Due to a lack of recursion depth limits when parsing deeply nested XML elements, processing such requests exhausts system stack memory and crashes the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An important-impact denial-of-service flaw exists in PHP's SOAP extension. When a SoapServer endpoint processes a specially crafted, deeply nested SOAP XML request, unbounded recursion in XML cleanup (and related decode/WSDL helpers) can exhaust the process stack and crash the PHP worker. Exploitation requires a reachable SoapServer that loads ext/soap; typical PHP applications that do not enable the SOAP extension or expose SoapServer are not affected by this attack path. Under PHP-FPM, repeated requests can exhaust the worker pool and take the application offline. Red Hat enterprise hardenings such as ASLR, NX, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and SELinux do not mitigate this stack-exhaustion DoS.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

If SoapServer is unused, disable or remove the SOAP extension (php-soap / extension=soap) so the vulnerable parser is not loaded. Restrict any exposed SoapServer endpoints to trusted clients using a host firewall or network segmentation. Process and cgroup resource limits may contain host impact but do not prevent PHP-FPM worker crashes or pool exhaustion from crafted nested SOAP requests.

vulnerabilities.title: php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's memory limit handling during request parsing. PHP records certain state as ready for use before all required memory allocations complete. If an allocation fails due to memory exhaustion, the incomplete state is not rolled back. Subsequent cleanup operations treat the uninitialized memory as valid, leading to memory corruption. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via crafted HTTP requests to achieve remote code execution against mod_php with default configuration, and against FPM through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Rated Important. An unauthenticated remote attacker could corrupt engine memory and potentially execute arbitrary code, but reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing. Standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM rather than mod_php. PHP-FPM workers exit on early initialization failures before reaching the corrupted structures, so remote code execution is difficult in practice and typically requires non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution.

vulnerabilities.title: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's error handling and worker process state management. PHP contains error handling, object, and extension state that is retained by the process but points to memory owned by a single request. A fatal error can interrupt an operation or cleanup phase before that state is reset. If PHP catches the failure and continues cleanup, or reuses the persistent worker for a subsequent request, a later operation may act on the stale state after its underlying memory has been released. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to achieve use-after-free and remote code execution against mod_php. FPM is conditionally affected through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory corruption leading to potential arbitrary code execution. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, PHP applications exposed to public networks handle incoming requests directly, so no prior authentication is needed to reach the vulnerable code. Exploitation requires hitting a precise out-of-memory condition during request processing, which keeps this below Critical.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP. An unauthenticated remote attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted request to an affected Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) server endpoint. Due to a lack of recursion depth limits when parsing deeply nested XML elements, processing such requests exhausts system stack memory and crashes the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An important-impact denial-of-service flaw exists in PHP's SOAP extension. When a SoapServer endpoint processes a specially crafted, deeply nested SOAP XML request, unbounded recursion in XML cleanup (and related decode/WSDL helpers) can exhaust the process stack and crash the PHP worker. Exploitation requires a reachable SoapServer that loads ext/soap; typical PHP applications that do not enable the SOAP extension or expose SoapServer are not affected by this attack path. Under PHP-FPM, repeated requests can exhaust the worker pool and take the application offline. Red Hat enterprise hardenings such as ASLR, NX, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and SELinux do not mitigate this stack-exhaustion DoS.
notes.title: Statement

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

If SoapServer is unused, disable or remove the SOAP extension (php-soap / extension=soap) so the vulnerable parser is not loaded. Restrict any exposed SoapServer endpoints to trusted clients using a host firewall or network segmentation. Process and cgroup resource limits may contain host impact but do not prevent PHP-FPM worker crashes or pool exhaustion from crafted nested SOAP requests.

vulnerabilities.title: php: php: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in SOAP parser

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's memory limit handling during request parsing. PHP records certain state as ready for use before all required memory allocations complete. If an allocation fails due to memory exhaustion, the incomplete state is not rolled back. Subsequent cleanup operations treat the uninitialized memory as valid, leading to memory corruption. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via crafted HTTP requests to achieve remote code execution against mod_php with default configuration, and against FPM through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: OOM bailout during request parsing leads to memory corruption and RCE
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Rated Important. An unauthenticated remote attacker could corrupt engine memory and potentially execute arbitrary code, but reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing. Standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM rather than mod_php. PHP-FPM workers exit on early initialization failures before reaching the corrupted structures, so remote code execution is difficult in practice and typically requires non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PHP's error handling and worker process state management. PHP contains error handling, object, and extension state that is retained by the process but points to memory owned by a single request. A fatal error can interrupt an operation or cleanup phase before that state is reset. If PHP catches the failure and continues cleanup, or reuses the persistent worker for a subsequent request, a later operation may act on the stale state after its underlying memory has been released. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to achieve use-after-free and remote code execution against mod_php. FPM is conditionally affected through application-stage paths.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: php: fatal error handling retains stale request state leading to use-after-free
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory corruption leading to potential arbitrary code execution. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, PHP applications exposed to public networks handle incoming requests directly, so no prior authentication is needed to reach the vulnerable code. Exploitation requires hitting a precise out-of-memory condition during request processing, which keeps this below Critical.

notes.text:
The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates RPM packages, included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL client using system CA store and cause such clients to connect to malicious sites.

Due to inability to only distrust specific intermediate certificates in all clients using the system CA store, root CA certificates of authorities that signed weak intermediate CA certificates are being removed.

notes.text:
The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates RPM packages, included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL client using system CA store and cause such clients to connect to malicious sites.

Due to inability to only distrust specific intermediate certificates in all clients using the system CA store, root CA certificates of authorities that signed weak intermediate CA certificates are being removed.

notes.text: Security update for libpcap
notes.title: Title of the patch

notes.text:
This update for libpcap fixes the following issues:

- CVE-2026-0799: the BPF interpreter does not validate values in BPF instructions that load/store a value from/to a
  scratch memory register and allows for OOB access (bsc#1279782).
- CVE-2026-6244: libpcap BPF interpreter for the 'div #k' and 'mod #k' ALU instructions does not check whether the
  immediate value is zero. In particular uncommon use cases a crafted filter program can cause a division by zero
  (bsc#1279595).
- CVE-2026-6554: libpcap BPF interpreter treats the offset in the 'ja L' BPF instruction implements looping via backward
  jumps, but it does not limit the number of loop iterations. Can cause infinite loop (bsc#1279584).
- CVE-2026-18238: `rpcap` client code that processes a `RPCAP_MSG_PACKET` message received from the server incorrectly
  validates its headers and allows for an OOB access (bsc#1279783).
- CVE-2026-18313: `rpcapd` allocates up to 65536 bytes per each `RPCAP_MSG_UPDATEFILTER_REQ` or `RPCAP_MSG_STARTCAP_REQ`
  message received from the client and never frees the memory (bsc#1279784).
- CVE-2026-31911: libpcap BPF interpreter calls abort() if it encounters a BPF instruction that has an invalid opcode.
  In particular uncommon use cases a crafted filter program can terminate the OS process (bsc#1279588).
- CVE-2026-31912: libpcap BPF interpreter detects neither reaching the end of the filter program buffer due to lack of a
  return instruction nor executing a jump instruction with an offset that translates to a pointer outside of the buff
  (bsc#1279593).

notes.text: In BPF instructions that load/store a value from/to a scratch memory register the register index is an unsigned 32-bit integer and must not exceed 15, but libpcap BPF interpreter does not validate the value.  In particular uncommon use cases a crafted filter program can cause the interpreter to try reading and writing the OS process memory in the 16GiB starting at the current stack frame on 64-bit architectures and in the entire address space on 32-bit architectures.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: The rpcap client code that processes a RPCAP_MSG_PACKET message received from the server incorrectly validates its headers.  A malicious server can send a crafted message and cause the client to treat up to 20 bytes of the client process memory beyond the end of the buffer as if it was a part of the captured packet.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: rpcapd can allocate up to 65536 bytes per each RPCAP_MSG_UPDATEFILTER_REQ or RPCAP_MSG_STARTCAP_REQ message received from the client, but it never frees the memory, so it leaks memory even under normal use.  A malicious client can cause the server to leak memory substantially faster.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: libpcap BPF interpreter calls abort() if it encounters a BPF instruction that has an invalid opcode.  In particular uncommon use cases a crafted filter program can terminate the OS process.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: libpcap BPF interpreter detects neither reaching the end of the filter program buffer due to lack of a return instruction nor executing a jump instruction with an offset that translates to a pointer outside of the buffer.  In particular uncommon use cases a crafted filter program can cause the interpreter to try reading the OS process memory in the 32GiB around the buffer on 64-bit architectures and in the entire address space on 32-bit architectures.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: libpcap BPF interpreter for the 'div #k' and 'mod #k' ALU instructions does not check whether the immediate value is zero.  In particular uncommon use cases a crafted filter program can cause a division by zero.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: libpcap BPF interpreter treats the offset in the 'ja L' BPF instruction as a signed integer to implement looping via backward jumps, but it does not limit the number of loop iterations.  A crafted filter program or the 'protochain' primitive used on a crafted network packet can cause the interpreter to loop infinitely.
